_doc: Object layer of the aerial encode. Paths are relative to the repo root. coco.keep: the COCO classes that can occur in aerial footage (indoor and household classes are what a closed vocabulary emits for objects it has no name for). world.prompts: YOLO-World prompt -> index token; the .onnx is exported with exactly these prompts, in this order (run.sh does it). merge_iou: overlapping boxes from either head are one object; the more confident label wins. track: an object in the next kept frame is the same object at IoU >= iou when the two crops look alike (HSV histogram correlation >= min_appearance; this is what stops a track jumping a cut) and the two labels are in one group (heads swap labels inside a group: truck/tank/boat), across up to max_gap missed frames. A label in no group is its own group. The object's class is the confidence-weighted vote over its frames. text: scene text is an object class. Tesseract (page segmentation psm) only locates it: words with conf >= min_conf that look like a stencil, grouped into lines, become 'text' boxes; Florence reads them. A text box at least host_containment inside another object's box gives that object its words (AMMO on a truck); one with no host (NORTH GATE) stays an object of its own; one Florence reads as empty is dropped. ocr: each object is read on up to `views` crops spread over its frames (the largest view is often not the one showing the lettering), and the words are merged; classes in skip are not read. The reader runs on its own thread while the object layer is still on later frames: an object is handed over the moment its track closes, and the door is called once per `batch` views (each call loads the model). objects: what makes an object a fact. The heads run low so tracks stay continuous; a triple needs corroboration, the rule the OCR words already follow: the object seen on min_frames survivors, or once at or above min_confidence (on drone_raw every false 'tank' and 'humvee' was one look under 0.30; real objects caught in one look were 0.47 and up). An uncorroborated object stays in objects.jsonl and the overlay, marked fact:false and painted grey, and emits no triple. beside_reach: two facts in one frame are beside each other when their boxes, each grown by beside_reach of its own width and height on every side, overlap; the encode then emits 'person beside tank' as a subject depicted by that frame, and person beside tank (both directions) once per clip. Beside is the picture's geometry, the strict reading: on drone_raw the FUEL stencil shares frames 318-320 with people who stand by another truck, and is beside none of them. 'Near' means the two are in one frame, and that is answered by the reasoning layer's join over the frames' depicts rows, not by the encoder.
